soil_moisture.interpretation: Root-zone soil moisture (19.8 mm/m) is below the configured dry threshold (25 mm/m). Water-demanding crops face elevated moisture deficits without canal/well irrigation.

precipitation.interpretation: Elevated dry-spell risk detected with 16 consecutive dry days and a 22.5 mm seasonal rainfall deficit. Crops without supplemental irrigation face moisture stress.

vegetation.interpretation: Satellite vegetation greenness is low (NDVI 0.21 < 0.25). This reflects post-harvest fallow exposed soil or sparse vegetation. Local confirmation is required.

bare_field_windows.interpretation: Bare-field window confirmed by 4 independent satellite signals: low canopy greenness (NDVI 0.21), depleted root-zone moisture (19.8 mm/m), and precipitation deficits. Topsoil is exposed to solar desiccation and erosion. A short-cycle cover or forage pulse crop is strongly recommended.

heat_stress.interpretation: Observed 38 heat-stress days (Tmax >= 35°C) and 0 frost-risk days (Tmin <= 2°C) during the summer transition. Sensitive flowering stages require thermal protection.

limitations: Gridded satellite and reanalysis observations (9 km to 50 km) represent regional spatial averages rather than field-level sensor measurements.
Optical NDVI observations are subject to cloud obscuration, atmospheric aerosol interference, and 16-day compositing intervals.
Soil moisture assimilation models rely on surface radiometry and land-surface modeling; actual root-zone moisture varies by local soil compaction and texture.
Ground verification of canal water rotation ('warabandi'), tube-well electric reliability, soil salinity, and pest outbreaks is mandatory before planting.
